title: dreamdeckgame
author: East-Tone4841
selftext:
**One month, three AIs, and a game called DreamDeck 🐉🎮**

Hey everyone!

I wanted to share my experience spending the past month building a game with three AI tools: Claude, GPT, and Gemini.

The best way to describe the experience? That three-headed dragon meme.

You probably know the one. Two serious-looking heads… and one head that seems to be having a completely different adventure.

Here’s how I’d cast them, based on my own experience:

🐉 **Head #1: Claude — the serious developer**

Claude gets the fierce, focused-looking head.

For coding, it’s been the one I’ve relied on most. I’d ask for something, and it would often work out the details, anticipate the next steps, and come back with a surprisingly complete result.

But if my request accidentally included the words “image,” “icon,” or “make it look nice”…

Oh boy. 😂

Let’s just say I learned to give Claude the engineering job and find someone else for the art direction.

🐉 **Head #2: GPT — the talented artist I have to keep an eye on**

GPT gets the suspicious-looking head. The one that looks like it might bite me if I look away.

Long coding tasks were a roller coaster for me. Things would drift, details would get lost, and I’d have to keep checking what was happening.

But design, visual polish, and image generation?

That’s where I kept getting those “wait… that actually looks amazing” moments.

Sometimes a short prompt was enough to get something beautiful. I’d spend ages trying to explain an idea, then discover that a much simpler request worked better.

🐉 **Head #3: Gemini — the cheerful friend keeping morale alive**

Gemini gets the goofy head.

Ask it anything, and it always has something to say. Getting from a helpful conversation to finished work was sometimes another story. 😂

But as company during a frustrating day? Excellent.

And encouragement? First place. Easily.

Sometimes, after staring at the same broken thing for too long, a little encouragement really does help.

Obviously, this is just my experience with the tasks and versions I used. Someone else could have a completely different dragon.

After a month of building, fixing, redesigning, and occasionally wondering what I’d gotten myself into, the result is **DreamDeck**, a tactical auto-battle card game.

It’s still a work in progress. I’m continuing to improve it and finish the 3D models for the characters. That part takes time—especially when generation limits decide the workday is over before I do. 😂

But it’s reached the point where I can share it and invite people to play. That feels pretty special.

If it sounds interesting, you can try it here:

[Play DreamDeck](https://dreamdeckgame.com/)

I’d love to hear what feels fun, what feels confusing, and what you think needs work.

Thanks for reading—and if you’ve built something with AI too, I’d love to hear what your three-headed dragon looks like.
